title: Dadaocheng & Dihua Street: River Trade to Heritage
subtitle: A walking journey through Taipei’s historic trading quarter where tea merchants, fabric sellers and temple-goers shaped the city’s cosmopolitan past
blurb: Улица Дихуа показывает город купцов: чай, ткани, узкие дома и ветер с реки Даньшуй.

microcopy.line: A walking journey through Taipei’s historic trading quarter where tea merchants, fabric sellers and temple-goers shaped the city’s cosmopolitan past

content.intro: Дадаочэн дает вторую ключевую грань Тайбэя — не государственную и не храмовую, а купеческую: фасады лавок, чай, ткани, городские боги и связь с рекой. Пользователь начнет читать узкие торговые дома, аркады, храмовые входы, рынки тканей и набережную как следы города, выросшего на речной логистике и сезонной торговле. Как Дадаочэн превратился из речного торгового узла в район памяти, дизайна и городского досуга, не потеряв роль живого рынка?
content.routeLogic: Маршрут идет от Ten Consecutive Buildings к Dadaocheng Wharf. Такой порядок сохраняет логику возвращенного guide pack: сначала задает главный городской контекст, затем ведет через ключевые остановки и завершает прогулку финальной точкой маршрута.
content.bestFor: спокойной прогулки по теме маршрута первого знакомства с районом или объектом тех, кто хочет читать город через видимые детали
content.notFor: маршрута без самостоятельного чтения места гонки по точкам без остановок тех, кому нужен только транспортный трансфер
content.beforeYouGo: This route wanders through busy neighbourhood streets and active religious sites – dress modestly, wear comfortable shoes and be prepared for crowds. Many shops close for lunch or on Sundays, so check opening times during your visit. The Yongle Market and theatre share a building; the market operates 10:00–18:00 Monday–Saturday and closes on Sunday【358761065926668†L252-L268】, while the theatre’s public areas are open 09:00–21:00 most days【795831228515098†L40-L49】. Xia‑Hai City God Temple opens daily 07:00–19:00【532392218414816†L178-L179】, but be respectful during rituals. The Gu Family Residence is a kindergarten today – you can only view its façade from the lane【105370638655104†L160-L178】. Finally, Dadaocheng Wharf is always open, but the container market operates later in the day (16:00–22:00 on weekdays, 12:00–22:00 at weekends)【23540202143293†L129-L139】.

stopList.name: Ten Consecutive Buildings
stopList.note: A row of ten connected merchants’ houses whose Baroque façades line the northern end of Dihua Street

content.context: Stand on the opposite (east) side of Dihua Street and take in the sweep of façades facing you. This uninterrupted row of ten shophouses marks the northern entry to the neighbourhood.
content.lookFor: A row of ten connected merchants’ houses whose Baroque façades line the northern end of Dihua Street
content.practical: Ориентир на месте: Ten Consecutive Buildings. Продолжайте к следующей точке маршрута.

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: In the 19th century, merchants rebuilt their timber storefronts in fired brick and embellished them with stucco scrolls and pediments, borrowing from European Baroque styles【915975356399163†L116-L170】. Each shop is long and narrow, with a commercial front room and living quarters above that open onto a rear loading lane; boatmen could haul tea, camphor or rice directly from the river to the back doors【83443692331992†L129-L133】. Today the row is a favourite spot for wedding photographs, yet it still hints at the scale of the Dadaocheng boom. Notice how the carved gables and pilasters echo each other across all ten units, suggesting the merchants’ desire to present a united front to visiting traders.

stopList.name: A.S. Watson & Co. Building
stopList.note: Historic Western‑style shophouse that once housed Taiwan’s first Watson’s pharmacy

content.context: Continue south to a three‑storey building faced in ochre brick and cream plaster. This was the early‑20th‑century branch of A.S. Watson & Co., a British pharmacy founded by Dr Thomas Boswell Watson.
content.lookFor: Historic Western‑style shophouse that once housed Taiwan’s first Watson’s pharmacy
content.practical: Ориентир на месте: A.S. Watson & Co. Building. Продолжайте к следующей точке маршрута.

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: Like its neighbours, the building follows the traditional shophouse plan – narrow frontage and deep interior – but its pseudo‑Baroque façade announces foreign influence with arched windows and balustrades【667390623570650†L92-L105】. When Dadaocheng was the epicentre of Taiwan’s tea trade, international firms like Watson’s clustered here to serve expatriates and wealthy Chinese merchants. Look for the carved company name on the pediment and imagine chemists dispensing tonics to a cosmopolitan clientele. The ground floor now houses a bookshop and café, showing how the street adapts its heritage buildings to contemporary uses.

photo.alt: Buildings along Dihua Street (A.S. Watson & Co.)

stopList.name: Xia‑Hai City God Temple
stopList.note: A tiny, gilded temple famed for matchmaking and anchored in the community since the 1850s

content.context: The temple’s roofline bristles with dragons and phoenixes. Built in 1859 by immigrants from Tong’an County【293774572970339†L134-L236】, it enshrines the City God, a deity charged with keeping order in the underworld, and has become a magnet for couples seeking love.
content.lookFor: A tiny, gilded temple famed for matchmaking and anchored in the community since the 1850s
content.practical: Ориентир на месте: Xia‑Hai City God Temple. Продолжайте к следующей точке маршрута.

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: Step inside to see the dense arrangement of altars, incense coils and carved beams. The building occupies only a few square metres – testament to high land prices during the trading boom – but its gilded carvings and ceremonial bells fill it with atmosphere. In front of the main altar, worshippers leave offerings and register their names on bamboo strips. A side altar to the Old Man Under the Moon attracts those hoping to meet a partner; you will see red strings and prayer slips tied to the grate. When you emerge, note how the temple sits flush between shopfronts: religion here is woven into the commercial fabric, offering blessings to merchants and sailors alike【915975356399163†L62-L148】.

stopList.name: Yongle Fabric Market
stopList.note: Multi‑storey market known for fabrics, tailor shops and a food court

content.context: Further south the street opens onto the bulk of the Yongle Market, a four‑storey building that replaced an earlier market destroyed by fire. The ground floor hosts hawkers selling spices, dried fruit and cooked snacks; upstairs hundreds of stalls display bolts of silk, cotton and lace.
content.lookFor: Multi‑storey market known for fabrics, tailor shops and a food court
content.practical: Ориентир на месте: Yongle Fabric Market. Продолжайте к следующей точке маршрута.

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: Locals come here to commission qipao dresses or to browse fabrics for home projects, and the air is thick with the sound of haggling and the clatter of sewing machines. The market’s institutional appearance belies a long continuity: Dadaocheng was a major centre for textile production during the Qing dynasty, and Yongle remains its commercial hub. Look for glimpses of the original stone foundations around the entrance. Remember that stalls close promptly at 18:00 and the market is shut on Sundays【358761065926668†L252-L268】, so plan your visit accordingly.

stopList.name: Dadaocheng Theater
stopList.note: Modern performance space promoting Taiwanese opera and folk arts on the upper floors of Yongle Market

content.context: Take the elevator in the north‑west corner of Yongle Market up to the eighth floor to reach the Dadaocheng Theater. Opened in 2010, this municipal venue is designed to nurture Taiwanese opera, glove puppetry and other traditional performing arts【874903677784180†L68-L85】.
content.lookFor: Modern performance space promoting Taiwanese opera and folk arts on the upper floors of Yongle Market
content.practical: Ориентир на месте: Dadaocheng Theater. Продолжайте к следующей точке маршрута.

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: The theatre’s lobby displays costumes and instruments and often hosts rehearsals open to passers‑by. Performances take place in a 226‑seat auditorium draped in crimson; you may catch a troupe tuning lutes or singers warming up in Minnan dialect. Built atop a utilitarian market, the theatre symbolises the neighbourhood’s renewed commitment to heritage – using modern infrastructure to sustain living traditions. Even if you do not see a show, the trip upstairs offers panoramic views over Dadaocheng’s tiled roofs. Note that public areas are usually open 09:00–21:00【795831228515098†L40-L49】, but the auditorium only opens when performances are scheduled.

stopList.name: Gu Family Residence (Koo House)
stopList.note: Red‑brick courtyard home of a wealthy tea merchant family, now viewed from the lane

content.context: Down a narrow lane off Guisui Street stands the Gu family residence. Built in the early 20th century, this two‑storey home mixes Minnan courtyard elements with Western baroque detailing: the red‑brick façade is ornamented with floral reliefs, while the interior (not open to the public) reputedly contains a central courtyard flanked by covered corridors【105370638655104†L160-L178】.
content.lookFor: Red‑brick courtyard home of a wealthy tea merchant family, now viewed from the lane
content.practical: Ориентир на месте: Gu Family Residence (Koo House). Продолжайте к следующей точке маршрута.

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: The Gu family amassed its fortune trading tea and rice during the Dadaocheng boom and was known for philanthropy; their home symbolised wealth and cosmopolitan taste. Today the building houses a kindergarten, so you can only view its exterior – please remain quiet and do not enter the premises. Stand at the lane entrance to appreciate the symmetrical façade and high archway and imagine the courtyard life of merchant elites in the 1920s.

stopList.name: Dadaocheng Wharf
stopList.note: Former riverport transformed into a riverside park and container market with sunset views

content.context: Finish your journey by following Guide Street west to the embankment. Before you is Dadaocheng Wharf, once the busiest point of embarkation for Taiwan’s tea exports.
content.lookFor: Former riverport transformed into a riverside park and container market with sunset views

deepDive.title: Подробнее
deepDive.body: In 1869 more than 120 thousand catties of Taiwanese oolong tea left this port for New York【293774572970339†L134-L236】, and for decades junks and barges jostled here for space. Today the warehouses have been cleared to create a riverside promenade with cycle lanes and a market made from repurposed shipping containers. On weekends, vendors sell craft beer, coffee and street food until late into the evening【23540202143293†L129-L139】; during the week it is quieter but open 24 hours for leisurely walks. Stand at the railing and look south to see Taipei’s modern skyline, then north to imagine the flat‑bottomed tea boats of the 19th century. The wharf symbolises the transformation of Dadaocheng from a working port into a space for leisure and reflection.
